newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech shares fall as early high cap rally fades.
newsitem.headline: Czech shares fall as early high cap rally fades.

text.p: The Prague bourse's PX50 and RPIX indices continued to move lower on Tuesday as an early rally from major issues faded away just after the start of continuous trading.

With CEZ and Ceska Sporitelna unchanged, SPT Telecom and Komercni Banka both lost five crowns to 2,990 and 2,145 respectively and dealers said the situation, especially with Komercni Banka, was even worse on the over-the-counter (OTC) market.
"Komercni is down to 2,070/2,090 on the OTC and at tomorrow morning's fixing it could easily be around 2,060 or 2,070," said Petr Koblic of Zivnostenska Banka.
Koblic said the market was being driven lower by an absence of interest from foreigners combined with little support from domestic investors. "This could go on for one or two more weeks," he said.
Apart from the heavily capitalised issues, smaller shares on the PX50 were also almost all down.

The biggest decliner was, ironically, north-Moravian brewer Radegast which on Tuesday posted sharply higher 1995 nine month gross profits of 281.5 million crowns from 230 million in the same period last year.
Radegast, which is 20 percent owned by Britain's Bass Plc, fell 237 crowns to 4,513.
